 COMMON JUDGMENT
These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
As all these petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 04.10.2023 at about 10.00 a.m,
when the petitioner in MVC.816/2024 was proceeding as pedestrian by the side of the road at Vaddarahalli,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, the driver of an car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913 came from Madanayakanahalli at high speed in a rash & negligent manner without observing the traffic rules, dashed against the petitioner in MVC.816/2024 from the back side and also dashed to the petitioner in MVC.817/2024 as she was standing by the side of the road.
Due to the impact both the petitioners were fell on the road and sustained injuries all over the body.
After the accident the petitioners were shifted to respective hospitals, treated accordingly and then discharged.

They were still under treatment and had spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance Priyanka R vs Jayaram H N on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157792133/
2 and other incidental expenses.

this Court will move through the initial documentary evidence.
The first stage of analysis concerns how the perpetrator was put into action.
The accident was occurred on 04.10.2023 at about 10.00 a.m.

The FIS was filed on the same day at about 3.30 p.m, by the petitioner himself when he was admitted in the M.J.Multispeciality hospital in the presence of Madanayakanahalli Police Station Head Constable No.311.
In the said FIS the registration number of the car in the accident is mentioned as KA-14-ML-3913.
The emphasis is at the inception itself the vehicle which was involved in the accident is mentioned.

It is relevant to note that on meticulous scrutiny of Ex.P.2 FIS, this Tribunal can lucidly observe that all the arithmetical numbers are mentioned in the English and in the complaint the vehicle number is mentioned as Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913.
This observation is made with a clear intent of having regarding to the contention urged by the petitioner in his statement and the same will be discussed in the later part of the judgment.

10. As this witness turned hostile, the learned counsel for insurance company sought permission to cross-examine him,
which was granted.

Despite cross-examination the insurance  11 SCCH-23  MVC.816/2024 C/w MVC.817/2024 company was not successful in establishing its defence regarding non-involvement of the insured car in the accident in question.
In other words, Investigating Officer withstood the test of cross-examination and explained in detail as to how the offending vehicle was traced by him.

It clears that accident took place from vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-MC-3913.

It is manifest from the evidence on record that now the dispute is with regard to actionable negligence.
A close look at the spot mahazar prima facie discloses that accident occurred in the manner as alleged by the petitioners in their respective petitions.
The history of the injuries mentioned in the wound certificates and the discharge summaries establish that the claimants sustained injuries in a Road Traffic Accident.
The IMV report goes to show that at the time of inspection no visible damages were found on the car.
Just because no damages were caused to the car, it cannot be concluded that it was not at all involved in the accident.

As per allegation it was dashed to the persons who was  12 SCCH-23  MVC.816/2024 C/w MVC.817/2024 Priyanka R vs Jayaram H N on 17 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157792133/

12. Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested the vehicle on road and found that its brake system were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the above said vehicle.
Therefore the driver of car did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he went and dashed against the petitioners in reverse manner leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
In the cross-examination of PW.1 & 2 the learned counsel for the insurance company could not elicit anything to negate their testimonies.
Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands.
At one stretch it denied the very involvement of its insured vehicle and at another it contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of petitioners.

Though the insurance company denied the cause of the accident as well as the very involvement of its insured vehicle,
it has not let in any cogent evidence to this effect.

Further,
the insurance company did not make any attempt to examine the driver of car, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-  14 SCCH-23
MVC.816/2024 C/w MVC.817/2024 examination of driver of car is fatal to the defence of insurance company.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW's.1 & 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the car.
With this observation issue No.1 (in all the petitions) is answered in the Affirmative.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
 "(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The  Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased  at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of  Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the  said claim, the injured claimant has not placed  any material on record, it is for the Courts and  Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The  notional income fixed by the Karnataka State  Legal Services Authority for the accident of the  year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any  material produced by the claimant to prove his  income, it is appropriate to assess the notional  income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per  month, and the same is assessed as the monthly  income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In other words, Investigating Officer withstood the test of cross-examination and explained in detail as to how the offending vehicle was traced by him.
The history of the injuries mentioned in the wound certificates and the discharge summaries establish that the claimants sustained injuries in a Road Traffic Accident.
The IMV report goes to show that at the time of inspection no visible damages were found on the car.
Just because no damages were caused to the car, it cannot be concluded that it was not at all involved in the accident.
It was dashed from rear side.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the above said vehicle.
Therefore the driver of car did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he went and dashed against the petitioners in reverse manner leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
